framework_note: Repo ships JAX/Haiku original + PyTorch reimplementation (tapnet/tapnext/tapnext_torch.py). Port from the PyTorch impl; JAX deps not needed.
architecture: ViT (Conv2d patch-embed 3->768 @8x8 + 12x TRecViTBlock, width=768, heads=12); each block's temporal mixing is a RecurrentBlock = Linear -> CausalConv1D -> RG-LRU (gated linear recurrent unit / SSM). Heads: coordinate_head (MLP->512), visible_head (MLP->1). Explicit online state: TAPNextTrackingState{step, query_points, List[RecurrentBlockCache(rg_lru_state, conv1d_state)]}.

input.per_step: [1,3,H,W] image + [1,Q,3] query_points + cached state (rg_lru_state, conv1d_state per block)
dynamic_dims: video length (handled by host state loop)
input.note: Fix HxW (256x256 or 480x480) and max Q with zero-padding for static-shape compile.

preprocess.resize: bilinear to [model_size, model_size] (256 for POC; 256/480 in repo)

output.name: coordinates
output.via: coordinate_head MLP->512 then decode (verify decode convention)

output.name: new_state
output.note: RecurrentBlockCache x12 (rg_lru_state, conv1d_state) = 24 cache tensors; fed back as inputs next step (host-side loop). step (frame counter) and query_points (constant) are step-graph INPUTS only, host-managed -- not echoed as outputs (echoing them produced pass-through Cast/Constant outputs the ONNX->MLIR converter could not resolve).

recurrence.type: linear gated RNN / SSM (RG-LRU, Mamba/Griffin family)
recurrence.inference_step: rnn_scan(x.shape[1]==1) => y = a*h0 + x; pure elementwise, no control flow, static graph (tapnext_lru_modules.py:102)
recurrence.state: RecurrentBlockCache(rg_lru_state, conv1d_state) per block; TAPNextTrackingState wraps list + step + query_points
recurrence.tpu_strategy: export per-step network (single-timestep path) to ONNX with static shapes; run recurrence/state loop on BM1688 host (C++/Python), feed cache back as ONNX input/output tensors

ref_sample: none (no existing point-tracker sample; ByteTrack/FearTracker are bbox trackers, different task). Nearest attention/transformer sample: sample/Qwen.
feasibility: FEASIBLE. Customer fear (recurrence not ONNX-exportable) is unfounded for inference: recurrence is LINEAR with an explicit single-step path (pure elementwise). Real work = (1) refactor forward to drive single-step online mode, (2) fix static shapes (HxW, max Q with padding), (3) choose ONNX export boundary (whole per-step forward incl cache as I/O), (4) host-side state loop in C++. Risks MEDIUM, not HIGH.
risks: Online single-step path must be driven explicitly (default demo runs whole-video parallel scan) - refactor forward()
num_query_points dynamic -> fix to max Q with zero-padding
CausalConv1D conv1d_state buffer handling in ONNX (fixed temporal_width=4)
Verify no data-dependent control flow in coordinate decode (coordinate_head outputs 512)

RESOLVED: nn.MultiheadAttention ONNX export. torch>=2.0 routes through aten::scaled_dot_product_attention (no symbolic); torch 1.13 routes through the fused aten::_native_multi_head_attention fast-path (also no symbolic at any opset, and EncoderBlock hits every fast-path gate in eval). Fix: monkey-patch nn.MultiheadAttention.forward onto its explicit F.multi_head_attention_forward (MatMul/Softmax/MatMul) path in tools/export_onnx.py (_mha_forward_exportable). Same math/weights, exports cleanly. Export venv: torch 1.13.1+cpu / torchvision 0.14.1+cpu / onnx 1.13.1 / onnxruntime 1.13.1 / numpy<2.

Checkpoint is a direct PyTorch state_dict (.pt) on GCS, ~2.4GB (401 keys, 244.5M params, Lightning 'tapnext.' prefix); torch.load(weights_only=False) + load_state_dict(strict=False), no JAX conversion

weights.format: PyTorch state_dict (.pt), loaded via torch.load(weights_only=False) + load_state_dict(strict=False); strips Lightning 'tapnext.' prefix. NO JAX/.npy conversion needed. ~2.4GB, 401 keys, 244.5M params.
